crates.name: bboxy450-harness
crates.scope: Finite two-turn/two-tool lifecycle; birth fencing A-B-A, unattended approval, FIFO control, bounded replay/lag/reset and Yarn arbitration. HTTP/TCP bytes, filesystem/process effects, wall-clock deadlines, secrecy and terminal bytes are witnessed by implementation tests; no arbitrary Rust refinement claim.
implementation_only: Embed-seat §3/§6 signal-path instruction/timing and kernel group/reap witnesses: tests/seat_process.rs + tests/support/seat_shutdown.rs, raw synchronous handlers and bounded atomic registry in process.rs. HarnessProcessLifecycle models hangup versus supervisor death for an arbitrary owned group; actual 100ms CPU scheduling, 250ms escalation, slot SC/CAS, PTY EOF classification and fsync are implementation evidence, not a real-time model

MCP §5 environment indirection: validate_environment rejects reserved references with ErrorClass::Config before startup; process::capture_stdout removes the namespace for all command resolvers. Immutable origin/data projection, no HarnessMcpServer lifecycle change; tests/seat_process.rs + tests/support/seat_launch.rs and the typed-error unit witness, controls bboxy-indirection/resolver-namespace

embed-seat §1/§6 and MCP §1/§5/§6 launch text, file parsing, source precedence and BBOXY environment projection: tests/seat_process.rs + tests/support/seat_launch.rs and engine/mcp unit witnesses; origin is immutable non-deserialized slot configuration, with no new HarnessMcpServer lifecycle transition
R22 automatic compaction: tests/context_auto.rs; finite abstraction excludes wire byte and blob durability
R23 ACP wire bytes, content merge, suffix repair and schema mapping: tests/acp_face.rs; HarnessAcpFlow covers FIFO/output ownership, not arbitrary Rust refinement
R24 MCP stdio, policy, timeout, crash and secrecy witnesses: tests/mcp_client.rs; HarnessMcpGroupClose covers group completion, actual signals and reaping remain process witnesses
R20 deterministic compaction and context replay: tests/context_compact.rs
R21 materialized fork and blob isolation: tests/store_fork.rs
runtime worker/permit hooks: tests/rt_budget.rs; timing measurements: make bench-budgets
real HTTP and UTF-8/SSE parsing

process groups and wall-clock limits
JSONL filesystem durability and blobs
secret redaction and terminal projection
GUI pixels/CoreText/Metal, native surface presentation and IME: tests/gui_render.rs and test-gui-smoke; no arbitrary Rust refinement claim
Protocol v0.2 optional identity heads, bounded Unicode terminal tails and snapshot repair: tests/gui_fixtures.rs + tests/fixtures/gui/v0_2-identity-terminal.jsonl
Real-clock GUI frame timing: tests/gui_bench.rs and make bench-gui-budget; UNMEASURED above ncpu
GUI applied delta ledger, completion and pre-completion snapshot repair: tests/gui_fixtures.rs; HarnessStreamToView models only dirty-wake bookkeeping
R24 MCP stdio, policy, timeout, crash and secrecy witnesses: tests/mcp_client.rs
Rich Markdown language equivalence, syntax-highlight colours, viewport glyph clipping and UI worker ownership: tests/gui_rich.rs + production headless smoke
Upgraded editor UTF-16/history/completion and approval keyboard navigation: tests/gui_rich.rs

contracts.name: HarnessTurnLifecycle
contracts.title: Exactly one ending; paired results at end; replay never redispatches; every queued turn eventually ends under weak fairness.
contracts.assumptions: Finite integer/Boolean model; two turns and tools, three births/log entries, bounded queues; named weak-fair action groups only. Replay drain abstracts a finite prefix atomically. Real HTTP, filesystem atomicity, kernel scheduling, monotonic time and terminal bytes remain implementation-only. No refinement proof.
contracts.property: Exactly one ending; paired results at end; replay never redispatches; every queued turn eventually ends under weak fairness.

contracts.name: HarnessProfileLoad
contracts.title: Closing a session joins pending profile IO without a late profile effect
contracts.assumptions: One profile operation, three births, one held completion. Named weak fairness on joining/retiring. Filesystem scheduling and kernel process-group timing remain implementation witnesses.
contracts.property: A stale or closed profile slot never changes session configuration; Close eventually joins it.

contracts.name: HarnessForkMaterialize
contracts.title: Publish a complete fixed parent prefix and its blobs atomically
contracts.assumptions: One fixed fork point, two parent heads, four materialization phases; crash may repeat forever, so no liveness claim. Actual rename, fsync, blob hashes, credentials and filesystem scheduling are implementation-only witnesses.
contracts.property: Visible child implies its blobs and fixed parent prefix are complete, regardless of subsequent parent appends.

contracts.name: HarnessControlLaneBound
contracts.title: A full work lane does not reduce the independent 256-slot control capacity
contracts.assumptions: Full 64-slot work lane; producer/consumer populations of 65 interrupt slots, 64 approval slots and one Close slot. Correct producers own and consumers return their type slot. The broken producer loses its reservation at full legitimate population and floods duplicates to depth 257 while consumers are delayed for this finite safety witness. FIFO and arbitrary malicious traffic remain implementation witnesses; no fairness claim.
contracts.property: Per-type slots are conserved, depth equals the outstanding op count, and the dynamically reachable legitimate maximum 130 fits the independent 256 capacity. The duplicate producer breaks slot conservation and overflows capacity.

contracts.name: HarnessProcessLifecycle
contracts.title: Cancel kills remaining members before releasing the leader reservation
contracts.assumptions: One arbitrary owned group stands for any tool, terminal or MCP group. The seat can receive hangup, then be killed by its supervisor before async cleanup. Hangup kills the group atomically before notifying async close; broken Hangup omits that kill. The 100ms/250ms OS deadlines and signal-handler instruction bounds are process/structural witnesses, not modeled real time. One leader (running/exited-waitable/reaped), one independent live member and one possibly escaped pipe holder. Leader exit, member exit, signal, reap, drain and cancel completion are separate actions. Weak fairness on exit/signal/reap/drain/end; OS waitid, real PID reuse and the 500ms grace remain process witnesses.
contracts.property: Cancel completion implies no live member. A signal never targets a group with neither a leader reservation nor a member; bounded drain eventually ends cancellation while the seat lives. After supervisor KILL no group member is alive. Abrupt seat death discharges the local join obligation; durable recovery is witnessed separately.

contracts.name: HarnessSubscriberReplayRegistration
contracts.title: Registration precedes the replay snapshot
contracts.assumptions: Three durable entries, one concurrent append, atomic registration and snapshot actions; kernel scheduling and actual socket delivery remain implementation witnesses.
contracts.property: No durable entry can fall between the replay snapshot and live registration.

contracts.assumptions: Produced/consumed counters 0..3, one wake bit, one drain phase. Weak fairness on frame drain/completion; broken control isolates safety. Real timing and OS wake delivery are API witnesses.
contracts.property: A budgeted frame never strands its remainder; arrival eventually yields a frame.

contracts.name: HarnessScrollStick

contracts.assumptions: Tail/offset/requested 0..3, one following flag, monotonic growth. Jump and wheel-to-bottom are atomic user actions; no user fairness assumed. Real layout clamp, wheel bursts and pixels remain implementation witnesses.
contracts.property: Tail follows append until manual scroll; Jump or wheeling to the bottom restores following.

contracts.name: HarnessEmbedLifecycle
contracts.title: Detaching a window/view preserves the actor; explicit Stop signals only its own birth.
contracts.assumptions: Three monotonic births with public A-B-A labels; delayed Stop captures a birth at admission. Detach drops the subscription; consume returns after its owned turn, then create drops Host. Dropped task handles preserve the actor. No liveness claim about arbitrary external IO. Old gateways are bound to old actors.
contracts.property: Detaching a window/view preserves the actor; explicit Stop signals only its own birth.

contracts.name: HarnessAutoCompact
contracts.title: Durable completed-turn reductions precede requests, are monotone across restart, and terminate.
contracts.assumptions: Load 0..4 abstracts exact compact-JSON estimation; one open turn in slot 3 above advancing completed frontiers 1..2; a queued cancellation may write latest ending 3 without closing that turn; trim estimates 2 or 3 explore trim-only and summary-without-new-trim, two durable frontiers and two ladder steps per round. Durable high-water frontiers represent log history. Weak fairness on ladder/send actions. Bytes, Unicode clipping, blob fsync and real process restart remain implementation witnesses; no arbitrary Rust refinement proof.
contracts.property: NeverReducesOpenTurn, BoundariesMonotone, ItemBeforeRequest and BoundaryEventuallySends.

contracts.name: HarnessMcpServer
contracts.title: An unavailable server never holds admission; requests timeout or finish, and results are fenced by birth.
contracts.assumptions: Three births (gen 0..2, public A-B-A) abstract the five-attempt product limit. A held response can cross two failures; a silent call needs Timeout. Failure and restart are independent of round admission. Weak fairness on admission, immediate failure/call and response/discard/timeout groups. SDK framing, real process groups, secrets, deadlines and pagination remain implementation witnesses; no arbitrary Rust refinement proof.
contracts.property: NoStaleResult, DeadIsFinal; RoundNeverWaits and CallEventuallyEnds under the named fairness assumptions.

contracts.name: HarnessAcpFlow
contracts.title: Session admission is FIFO, and a paused writer cannot close the face or hold the engine.
contracts.assumptions: One prompt followed by cancel; two engine events and two connection replies, queue 0..2 abstracts capacity 256. EngineNeverWaits is enabledness of the actual EngineEmit guard, including writer capacity in broken C; its witness compares actual successor edges at full capacity. Reading resumes under weak fairness, with a drain opportunity in every nonempty readable interval. Fair admission, engine, projection and writer actions; finite inbound burst. Durable prompt admission abstracts lag recovery; actual 4096-slot overflow and held-EOF replay are unit witnesses in src/frontends/acp.rs. Wire bytes, actual OS scheduling, dropped-delta repair and multi-session dispatch remain API witnesses. Pairing remains HarnessTurnLifecycle; no Rust refinement claim.
contracts.property: CancelHitsItsPrompt, CloseOnlyOnEof, EngineNeverWaits and PromptEventuallyResponds.

contracts.name: HarnessMcpGroupClose
contracts.title: Close joins every member of its process group even when SIGTERM is ignored.
contracts.assumptions: One unreaped leader and zero to two members; SIGTERM is ignored. Grace expiry abstracts the timer and sends SIGKILL, then leader wait completes Close. Members may exit independently before completion. Weak fairness on kill/reap after Close begins. Group ownership and pgid reuse remain HarnessProcessLifecycle; OS signals, EOF and reaping are process witnesses, not arbitrary Rust refinement. Maps to src/mcp.rs::finish_child and the stubborn_group fixture.
contracts.property: NoMemberAfterClose and ReapAfterKill; CloseEventuallyCompletes. Broken control kills only the leader, leaving a live member at completed Close.

contracts.name: HarnessGuiMarkdownBudget
contracts.title: Streaming parse work stays linear and deferred source bytes remain readable
contracts.assumptions: Seven streamed byte units plus a final byte introduced by completion; parser cost upper-bounded by source size, retained prefix and literal pending tail. The final byte cannot be visible before completion. Three-times-input parse credit plus one completion flush bounds total work by four times input. Render is enabled only for a dirty row. Completion dirties the row. Weak fairness on enabled rendering after completion; the suppressed-render control disables this step after completion. Actual Markdown equivalence, highlighting, CPU time and worker/UI ownership remain implementation witnesses, not a Rust refinement proof.
contracts.property: ParseWorkIsLinear; NoHiddenBytes; completed replies eventually become fully visible.

contracts.name: HarnessGuiApprovalChoice
contracts.title: A retired rendered approval cannot dispatch to the replacement prompt
contracts.assumptions: Three distinct sequential prompt ItemIds; replacement retires the previous prompt. Capture and dispatch are separate actions. Concurrent independent prompts and actual FIFO gateway delivery are implementation witnesses.
contracts.property: NoRetiredPromptDispatch
